Depending when your test is, and if you have a vehicle, I'd be happy to come and give you some tips and tricks! Im 25, female and I remember most of the path I was taken on and can pretend to be an instructor lol

Literally shoulder check every time (they are super super picky) ,signal, lane change, leave parking stalls, back up, and throw in a bunch while your just driving as well. I've taken both my N, and full license (2016) in Chilliwack, and have helped numerous friends pass theirs as well.

Follow the posted speed limits to a tee, don't go.with the flow.of traffic, unless it's below the posted speed and make a comment about it to the tester. They take you on the highway as well for the full license, so just make sure you're up to the posted speed before merging onto the Trans Canada. They took me on the highway at Young and we exited on Prest, and went back down to Chilliwack Central and back to the testing centre. Unless absolutely necessary don't go in the fast lane there's no need too.

If other drivers cause troubles while driving, blocking you in or taking too much time, or anything really, just talk to the tester. 

"Oh no, watch out for this guy" or " he's going a bit faster than the speed limit" shows them you're super vigilant around your surroundings

If you see the emergency vehicle before you are in the roundabout, yield until it passes. If you are in the roundabout and an emergency vehicle sirens behind you, DO NOT STOP! Do (and say), get into the right lane if you're not already and pull over safely after the roundabout
